name: Amiibank
subtitle: amiibo backups and N2 slots
promotionalText: Pick a game, check off the amiibo you own, and load them onto your N2 Elite in one go.
description: Amiibank keeps your amiibo backups on your iPhone and puts them to work.
• Import .bin backups one at a time or hundreds at once from Files
• Browse with pictures, filter by set, series, game or type, and see what you're missing
• Keep count of how many times you've written each one
• Scan your N2 Elite and see every slot at a glance, with the active one up front
• Add an amiibo to the next free slot, replace a slot, or save a slot back to your collection
• Pick a game, check off the amiibo you own, and load them all onto the N2 in one go
• Write a backup to a blank NTAG215 tag
• Every Switch, 3DS and Wii U game that reads amiibo, and what each amiibo does in it
• Save your collection to Game Center and restore it on another iPhone. Saves from different devices merge, so nothing gets lost.
No accounts, no ads, no tracking. Free and open source under the MIT license.

Amiibank needs an iPhone with NFC. Writing blank tags needs a key file you supply; Amiibank doesn't include one. Amiibank is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. amiibo is a trademark of Nintendo.
reviewNotes: Amiibank manages amiibo backup files the user already has, and writes them to NFC hardware the user owns.

Without NFC hardware: the Collection, Games and Settings tabs all work. The app ships the public AmiiboAPI catalog, so Collection lists every amiibo under Missing and Games lists every game that reads amiibo. Tap any amiibo for details and the games that use it.

With hardware: the N2 tab reads and writes an N2 Elite (a rewritable NFC tag with 200 slots), and Write to blank tag writes a blank NTAG215 sticker or card. Writing a blank tag also needs a key file that the user imports from their own device. Amiibank does not include, download or link to key files.
Game Center is used only for saved-game backups of the user's own collection. No login or account is required. The app collects no data.
